messages:
emily_sales: Hey team — Prospect (Veridian Health) asked for a CAIQ and SOC2 evidence pack as part of the POC. They also want confirmation we can support BYOK/KMS for isolated keys. timeline: they need an initial response by EOD Wed. Can security own the intake + evidence list?
emily_sales: Quick context: POC will run on Dedicated for 4 weeks, estimated 2 GPUs. Sales asked about egress restrictions and SLA during POC.
sam_security: I can pick this up. Can you drop the CAIQ they provided? need to see which sections map to our docs. Also note: BYOK for Dedicated == customer-managed keys in KMS/backplane or HSM?
emily_sales: Uploaded their CAIQ PDF and example vendor questionnaire to the thread. Link: https://drive.redwood/Veridian/CAIQ2026.pdf
jordan_se: FYI, the Dedicated offering supports KMS integrations (GCP/KMS, AWS KMS) and we have an HSM option for Private. For the POC we can enable a tenant-level KMS key if customer agrees. Need SRE to confirm network egress policy.
tarun_sre: We can lock down egress to whitelist IPs and block external hosts. For BYOK we'll need a short runbook: key import flow, rotation windows, and ops access policy. I can draft it.
emily_sales: Customer asked: will providing BYOK add time to POC start? they want start next Monday.
sam_security: If they insist on HSM-backed BYOK and an air-gapped on-prem connector, that will add weeks. If they accept cloud-KMS with customer key, we can do same-week. I'll list required evidence: SOC2 report, pen-test summary, encryption architecture diagram, KMS key lifecycle doc, supplier risk attestation.
kelsey_pm: @sam_security please also add expected risk exceptions for endpoint RDP/SSH and any required customer firewall rules. We should call out who owns remediation if any control gaps appear during review.
sam_security: On it. Draft evidence checklist: 1) SOC2 Type II attest (latest), 2) CAIQ answers (we'll prefill redwood responses), 3) Pen-test summary (last 12 months), 4) Encryption in transit + at rest diagram, 5) KMS integration guide (how keys are injected), 6) Data retention & deletion policy, 7) Access control matrix, 8) Incident response runbook + contact.
emily_sales: perfect — can you mark which items we can share immediately vs need redaction/exec approval? Also need a short blurb I can send to Veridian about POC SLAs and backup window.
sam_security: Immediate: CAIQ prefills, KMS guide (ops-level), encryption diagram (general). Need redaction/approval: SOC2 full report (share under NDA), pen-test with vuln details (share summary only). I'll annotate in Drive.
jordan_se: For SLA during POC: 99.5% uptime, best-effort support with on-call pager for severe incidents. If they want 24/7 enterprise SLA that requires dedicated contract. emily_sales — want me to draft that blurb?
emily_sales: yes please. Also ask Veridian whether they need data residency in-region — their security lead pinged that yesterday.
tarun_sre: One more ops note: if they want KMS key material uploaded to our cluster, we need IAM roles and a key policy that forbids Redwood admin export. That will be part of the runbook.
sam_security: I'm assigning the intake task in the security tracker to myself and will flag any high-risk items. Evidence-bot: please attach the redwood CAIQ template v2.
evidence-bot: Attached: redwood-CAIQ-template-v2.docx (uploaded)
emily_sales: Thanks all. Next steps: @sam_security to post final evidence checklist + notes by tomorrow noon; @jordan_se to draft POC SLA blurb; @tarun_sre to create KMS runbook draft. I'll follow up with Veridian about data residency and whether they accept cloud-KMS.
sam_security: Copy that. If anyone hears security-specific Qs from Veridian, tag me. I'll aim to have first draft by 11:30am tomorrow. :thumbsup:
emily_sales: Great — will update the customer. :rocket:
